import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a bar chart to compare the number of cameras in each sensor type
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.countplot(x='sensor_type', data=data, order=data['sensor_type'].value_counts().index)
plt.title('Distribution of Sensor Types')
plt.xlabel('Sensor Type')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.xticks(rotation=90)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot to compare megapixels and price
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.scatterplot(x='megapixels', y='price_usd', data=data)
plt.title('Relationship Between Megapixels and Price')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)')
plt.xscale('log')
plt.yscale('log')
plt.savefig('output2.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a histogram to compare the distribution of prices
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.histplot(data['price_usd'], bins=50, kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of Prices')
plt.xlabel('Price (USD)')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.xscale('log')
plt.savefig('output3.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
